To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in small‐for gestational age fetuses, the single deepest pocket was a more reliable predictor of fetal distress than the amniotic fluid indices.

1) the single deepest pocket is more sensitive and specific than the amniotic fluid in predicting fetal distress and 2) a single deepest pocket of 2 cm or less and an amniotic fluid of 2 cm are associated with fetal distress.

in the case of small‐for‐ gestational age fetuses, the amniotic fluid indices and single deepest pocket are not reliable predictors of fetal distress, but the amniotic‐fluid index is more reliable than the single deepest pocket.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between reduced amnionic fluid volume and increased fetal risk of distress in small‐ for‐gestational age pregnancies.
the relationship between the amniotic fluid indices, the single deepest pocket (SDP) and the amniotic index (A/I), and their ability in the prediction of fetal distress in SGA fetuses.
the development of a new method for measuring the amniotic fluid in the pregnant uterus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence to support a role of the amniotic fluid in the development of the human fetus.
the use of amniotic fluid indices in the diagnosis and monitoring of fetal well‐being in high‐risk pregnancies should be abandoned.

the amniotic fluid is a complex fluid, with the composition and properties of which are determined by the balance of the production, absorption and distribution processes, and that the volume of amniotic fluid in the normal pregnancy is determined by the balance between the production and the absorption processes, and that it is the volume of amiotic fluid that is important, rather than its constituents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the single deepest pocket is more sensitive than amniotic fluid in predicting fetal distress.
the amniotic fluid indices were significantly associated with the risk of fetal distress and were better than the single deepest pocket in predicting fetal distress.
the amniotic fluid is an important component of the amniotic cavity, which plays a crucial role in fetal development.

the amniotic fluid indices are not a good predictor of fetal distress in the setting of small for gestational age.
